title: HilbertA: Hilbert-Curve–Aligned Sparse Attention for 2D Structured Data
claim: Contiguous blocks ignore 2D neighborhoods, while 2D-local patterns preserve spatial locality but scatter attention into non-contiguous memory.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right; token grid beside two attention matrices, dashed divider
description: The left panel shows a parrot photo divided into a 4x4 grid of numbered tokens, 1 to 16 in raster order, under the title '2D Image Tokens'. A dashed vertical line separates it from the right side, titled 'Image Token Attention Map'. The right side has two 16x16 query-key matrices, each with Q on the left and K on top. In the first matrix, labeled 'Contiguous Sparse Attention Pattern', four colored 4x4 blocks (blue, orange, green, purple) run along the diagonal. In the second, labeled '2D-Local Sparse Attention Pattern', the same four colors appear as scattered 2x2 blocks in a checkerboard-like layout. The colors presumably map to spatial neighborhoods of the image. The eye goes first to the colorful matrices. The figure appears to be cut off at the bottom, and it shows no Hilbert-curve method.
caption: Image token layouts with their corresponding sparse
abstract: Designing sparse attention for 2D image data in diffusion and vision-language models requires reconciling spatial locality with hardware-efficient execution: handcrafted 2D sparsity patterns preserve spatial structure but often induce uncoalesced memory access, limiting practical speedups on modern GPUs. We present HilbertA , a 2D-aware sparse attention mechanism that reorders image tokens along a Hilbert curve, converting local spatial neighborhoods into contiguous memory segments for efficient GPU execution. To enable communication beyond local tiles, HilbertA shifts attention windows along the Hilbert-ordered sequence across layers and uses a small central shared region, preserving contiguous access while supporting cross-tile information flow. Across diffusion and vision-language models, HilbertA delivers consistent efficiency gains while maintaining competitive quality, achieving up to 4.16× attention acceleration and 1.44× end-to-end speedup on Flux.1-dev, and up to 2.30× attention acceleration with 1.57× faster time-to-first-token on Qwen3-VL-8B inference.
